title: Who’s News: Strategic Appointments at PsiQuantum, EigenQ, Qunova Computing, and Optica Quantum - Quantum Computing Report
gist: PsiQuantum adds Atomico/Skype founder Niklas Zennström to its board on top of a recently rebuilt C-suite (Victor Peng as CEO) while building fault-tolerant facilities in Chicago and Brisbane; EigenQ staffs up cryptography and security leadership ahead of a SPAC merger with Silicon Valley Acquisition Corp. (Nasdaq: SVAQ); and Korea's Qunova hires a CFO plus pharma and automotive R&D veterans to chase materials-simulation customers.

insights.claim: PsiQuantum appointed Niklas Zennström — Founder and CEO of Atomico and co-founder of Skype — to its Board of Directors effective August 11, 2026, replacing Siraj Khaliq as Atomico's board representative, signalling that Atomico is escalating the seniority of its oversight of the photonic quantum company.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A marquee European VC founder taking the board seat personally is a tell that PsiQuantum is being groomed for a large late-stage round or exit; watch Atomico's follow-on participation.
insights.quote: PsiQuantum has appointed Niklas Zennström to its Board of Directors, effective August 11, 2026.

insights.claim: PsiQuantum has recently installed an entirely operator-grade executive layer — Victor Peng as CEO, Rob Soderbery as Executive Vice President, and Sriram Sitaraman as Chief Information Officer — indicating a shift from research-led to execution- and scale-led management.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hiring semiconductor/enterprise operators rather than physicists usually precedes commercial delivery milestones or capital-markets events; treat it as a timeline indicator for the photonic FTQC roadmap.

insights.claim: PsiQuantum is simultaneously constructing fault-tolerant quantum computing facilities in Chicago and Brisbane, making it one of the few quantum firms with heavy physical infrastructure committed on two continents.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Two-site capex on this scale implies anchor public funding (Illinois and Australia) and creates a regional supply-chain and construction spend to track.
insights.quote: PsiQuantum’s ongoing construction of fault-tolerant quantum computing facilities in Chicago and Brisbane
insights.locator: The appointment coincides with PsiQuantum’s ongoing construction

insights.claim: EigenQ, Inc. is preparing a proposed merger with Silicon Valley Acquisition Corp. (Nasdaq: SVAQ), giving public-market investors a near-term listed vehicle exposed to quantum-safe cryptography.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A named ticker (SVAQ) is a directly tradable expression of the post-quantum cryptography theme; watch the merger vote and any redemption pressure.
insights.quote: as the company prepares for its proposed merger with Silicon Valley Acquisition Corp. (Nasdaq: SVAQ)
insights.locator: Truskovsky previously served as Vice President of Cryptography

insights.claim: EigenQ named Mark Pecen — co-founder of the Quantum-Safe Cryptography Working Group at ETSI and formerly an EigenQ board member and strategic advisor — as Vice Chairman, importing standards-body credibility into the company's leadership.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Standards-committee insiders as executives is how crypto-migration vendors win procurement; a leading indicator of EigenQ's government and telco pipeline.
insights.locator: EigenQ, Inc. has appointed Mark Pecen as Vice Chairman

insights.claim: EigenQ created a Chief Information Security Officer role for the first time, promoting Alexander Truskovsky from Vice President of Cryptography to own global cybersecurity strategy, risk management and product compliance ahead of the SPAC transaction.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Newly created compliance-facing C-suite roles are standard pre-listing scaffolding; read it as confirmation the merger is on a live timetable.
insights.locator: promoted Alexander Truskovsky to the newly created role

insights.claim: Qunova Computing appointed Jake Hwang — previously Chief Strategy Officer and Chief Business Officer at Nearthlab — as Chief Financial Officer and Board Member, adding financial and strategy leadership to a Korean quantum software firm.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Bringing in a CFO with a board seat typically precedes a fundraise or listing attempt in Korea's quantum sector.
insights.locator: Qunova Computing has expanded its executive leadership

insights.claim: Qunova hired business development executives drawn from pharmaceutical and automotive R&D — Evan Kang with over 20 years at SK Chemicals and LG Chem, and Woomin Kyoung with nearly three decades at Hyundai Motor Company's R&D Division leading materials simulation and CFD — showing quantum software go-to-market is now aimed at chemicals, pharma and auto engineering budgets rather than research grants.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hiring domain sellers from Korean chaebol R&D units signals where the first paying quantum-simulation contracts are expected; watch for SK/LG/Hyundai pilot announcements.
insights.quote: nearly three decades of engineering experience from Hyundai Motor Company’s R&D Division to lead materials simulation and CFD initiatives
insights.locator: Kang brings over 20 years of pharmaceutical R&D

insights.claim: Optica Publishing Group named NIST Fellow Kartik Srinivasan — Co-Director of the NIST/University of Maryland Joint Quantum Institute and Deputy Editor since the journal launched in 2023 — as Editor-in-Chief of Optica Quantum, succeeding founding editor Michael G. Raymer.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Editorial control of the field's photonics-quantum journal moving to a NIST insider tightens the US standards-research nexus; useful for tracking which modalities get institutional airtime.
insights.locator: Optica Publishing Group has appointed Kartik Srinivasan
